algorithm: DSTU 9041:2020 full encrypt/decrypt worked example, Annex G.1 (l(p)=256)
source: docs/papers/DSTU_9041-2020.pdf, Annex G.1 (Додаток Г.1) - see docs/pseudocode/dstu9041.md for verification detail
hash_function: Kupyna-256 (DSTU 7564:2014), truncated to l_H=32 bits taken from the LOW-order end of the digest (confirmed empirically against hazmat::kupyna::Kupyna256 - the standard's own clause 5.7 states the truncation direction abstractly, not which end of a concrete byte string that means)
private_key_e_note: Annex G's own convention: every parameter in these worked examples is hex, 4 bits per hex digit, even bare small integers with no local label - 0x25 = 37 decimal. Confirmed: scalar_mult(37, P) == Q exactly. An earlier verification pass misread this as decimal 25 and flagged a false 'erratum' before catching the same hex convention it had already found for d=0x18 - see docs/DECISIONS.md D-163's addendum.
kalyna_kw_input_note: The Kalyna-256/256-KW input that reproduces the printed t below is M' padded with one additional all-zero 256-bit block (M' || 0x00*32), NOT M' alone - M' alone is exactly one 256-bit Kalyna block, but the printed ciphertext only reconciles against a 2-block (64-byte) KW input. Why DSTU 9041 requires this second block is not yet resolved - see docs/pseudocode/dstu9041.md's open-gap note. Recorded as an empirical fact needed to reproduce the vector, not yet explained from a cited clause.
t_ciphertext_note: The standard's own printed t is missing a single hex digit ('0' dropped between ...B3CE and F710...) - a real single-character erratum in the published Annex Г.1, confirmed by inserting it back and getting an exact 192-hex-digit (96-byte) match against Kalyna256_256Kw::wrap's own computed output for the plaintext/key above. t_ciphertext_hex here is the CORRECTED value (with the missing digit restored), not the literal printed text.
verified_checks: P, Q, R, T all satisfy the curve equation
R == 7 * P (ephemeral key applied to base point)
T == 7 * Q (ephemeral key applied to public key)
37 * P == Q (private key e=0x25=37, hex convention)
Kupyna256(l_M~(16 bits) || M~(200 bits)) truncated to its last 4 bytes == the stated H = BF8B8620, via hazmat::kupyna::Kupyna256
Kalyna256_256Kw::wrap(kappa, M'||0x00*32) == t_ciphertext_hex above (after restoring the standard's own dropped hex digit), via hazmat::kalyna_kw::Kalyna256_256Kw - this project's own implementation
open_question: Why the Kalyna-KW input needs a second all-zero 256-bit block appended to M' (bringing it to 2 blocks / 64 bytes) is not yet resolved from the scanned clauses - clauses 6.5-6.12 and the exact wording of clause 11 that would explain this are not in the current scan. Treat kalyna_kw_input_note above as an empirical fact, not yet a cited requirement.
